goal: Contain source-originated per-file failures without corrupting protocol framing, aborting unaffected work, or destroying a valid destination copy.
recommended_approach: Use the proposed contract-v7 need ledger, per-socket lanes, same-handle validation, exact-size shard buffering, explicit skip and record terminators, and staged atomic commits, while adding bounded staging admission and ownership- and cancellation-safe stage cleanup.
comparison: The change selects the right protocol and transactional primitives and closes the major earlier design gaps, but its staging resource and lifecycle rules can still cause avoidable fatal failures or interfere with concurrent transfers.
material_changes: Add destination-scoped byte admission for concurrent staged records.
Prevent mirror deletion from treating another session's live staging files as ordinary extraneous files.
Make staging cleanup cancellation-safe through an ownership guard that runs when a record writer is dropped.

findings.title: Concurrent staging can manufacture an avoidable fatal disk-full failure
findings.evidence: docs/plan/SOURCE_SIDE_CONTAINMENT.md:620 — the plan acknowledges that aggregate stages can exceed available space but explicitly omits admission control.
findings.predicted_failure: A destination with enough space to replace each file sequentially but not all concurrent records can hit ENOSPC and abort the session even though throttling would complete successfully.
findings.better_approach: Reserve each record's declared size through a destination-scoped weighted budget before creating its stage, release it on commit or abort, and reduce concurrency when free-space headroom is tight.

findings.title: A mirror session can delete another session's live staging file
findings.evidence: docs/plan/SOURCE_SIDE_CONTAINMENT.md:627 — the plan rejects prefix cleanup because it could delete another concurrent session's stage, yet line 632 delegates cleanup to the ordinary mirror pass; crates/blit-core/src/mirror_planner.rs:342 deletes every destination entry absent from the source set.
findings.predicted_failure: While one transfer is writing a stage, a concurrent mirror can classify it as extraneous and unlink it; the first transfer then fails its rename or loses the staged inode, and the supposedly contained file does not land.
findings.better_approach: Either serialize transfers targeting the same canonical destination root or give stages durable session ownership with a live lease that mirror planning excludes; reap only stages whose ownership is proven stale.

findings.title: Cancellation bypasses the explicit abort cleanup path
findings.evidence: docs/plan/SOURCE_SIDE_CONTAINMENT.md:365 — RecordWriter cleanup is specified only through an explicit abort method, while crates/blit-core/src/remote/transfer/abort_on_drop.rs:84 aborts receive tasks by dropping their futures.
findings.predicted_failure: CancelJob, disconnect, or an adjacent task failure can drop an active writer without calling abort, leaving a visible staging file indefinitely on non-mirror transfers and feeding the concurrent-mirror race.
findings.better_approach: Wrap every stage in an RAII ownership guard that removes its exact path on Drop and is disarmed only after a successful rename; add cancellation tests for in-stream, data-plane, and local routes.
